QualityControlProtocol.metaTitle: Quality Control Protocol | Digital Dental Lab
QualityControlProtocol.metaDescription: Structured quality control protocol for digital prosthetic workflows: file validation, margin control, contact verification, occlusion validation, implant passivity checks, and final inspection.
QualityControlProtocol.title: Quality Control Protocol
QualityControlProtocol.intro: This protocol defines the release criteria for digitally designed prosthetic cases. Each validation step is designed to reduce chairside adjustment load, improve insertion predictability, and maintain repeatable outcomes across clinicians and case types.

step1.title: 1. File Validation
step1.text: Input files are reviewed for mesh integrity, missing data zones, registration confidence, and scan noise in critical areas (margin perimeter, proximal interfaces, posterior occlusal anatomy).
step1.impact: Prevents geometry inference errors that commonly cause seating resistance and high-point corrections during insertion.

step2.title: 2. Margin Inspection
step2.text: Finish lines are inspected for continuity, readability, and stable transition geometry. Ambiguous regions are flagged for clarification before design finalization.
step2.impact: Reduces internal binding and marginal mismatch that force intraoral grinding or remakes.

step3.title: 3. Contact Verification
step3.text: Proximal contacts are controlled against case-specific targets by tooth position, restorative span, and insertion path constraints. Over-tight contact profiles are corrected at design stage.
step3.impact: Lowers contact-related insertion friction and decreases chairside proximal adjustment time.

step4.title: 4. Occlusion Validation
step4.text: Static and dynamic occlusal checks are performed using calibrated contact thresholds, antagonist morphology assessment, and functional path verification before CAM release.
step4.impact: Reduces premature contacts and limits post-insertion occlusal corrections.

step5.title: 5. Implant Passivity Checks
step5.text: Implant-supported designs undergo passivity-oriented framework verification, connection alignment control, and interface consistency checks before finalization.
step5.impact: Minimizes strain-inducing misfit patterns and reduces mechanical complications related to forced seating.

step6.title: 6. Final Inspection
step6.text: Final inspection confirms release against protocol checklist: fit control, morphology consistency, contact plan compliance, surface quality, and case traceability documentation.
step6.impact: Standardizes delivery quality and decreases variability in insertion behavior between cases.

QualityControlProtocol.whyTitle: Why This Matters for Your Clinic

whyPoints.one: Reduced chairside correction load improves schedule stability.
whyPoints.two: More predictable insertion lowers procedural stress in complex appointments.
whyPoints.three: Standardized validation supports repeatable outcomes across clinicians.
whyPoints.four: Clear release criteria improve technical communication and shorten decision loops.
